author: antraxia
text:
Hey muffles,

Been a while since I posted: I've tried to keep it down to a dull roar
concerning the great stuff on this chart. First look at how the edge of
 that flag to the left is still holding down price and it coincides with
 a smaller qm level and an order cluster at that level which is the
entrance to compression and it has a smaller qm in it on the LTF and it
has possibly broken into HTF comp lower etc. That is a smashing place
to look for trades :).

The second QM level provided a great op as well but you would have to
wait for PA and then follow it level by level on the way down as its at
target on this scale Edit: (on closer inspection check out where that
swing stopped on H1 I guarantee IF took this one too :) see if you can
work out why). If you held you could get out at the next target which
price snogged and then buggered off to continue the higher scale trend.

Hopefully that helps a bit with your question. Notice that I've kind of
 avoided the FL question on this so see if the one you marked is strong
enough to indicate a change in scale vs the engulf into the comp below.
 There are other things on here I've likely left off so others feel free
 to add you to IF :) Thanks to everyone for the continuing growth.
Cheers.

Gaf

P.S. I've left off a few important FL that got engulfed on the way
down. This would be a better reason than entrance into compression as I
 always find that a bit dodgy. Sorry for the lack of detail.

author: juniormaiafx
text:
smimon wrote: If you don't mind,
 I'd like to ask you something IF for clarification, that's been a
source of mild confusion to me for some time.

In the diagram (very simplified), there are 2 FO scenarios. Scenario 1
is very clear, and predictable FO. Scenario 2 however - price engulfs
the seemingly more important FL, and bounces from a more minor one. Is
this a valid FO, and we should therefore treat the resultant move north
with the same significance as if it had originated from the important
FL? Or is this genuine engulf south?

Let's say for arguments sake in scenario 2, the "important" high is the
top of the last significant downward FTR of a bear move before reversal
north - so not just a random high, but an important level.

Thanks for any help, even if it's just a cryptic comment ;-)

author: Kovalenko
text:
Hi IF

First - Happy new year ! I hope you are well.

I would like to hear your attitude to median lines analyzing a chart.

Many traders use this method . What do you think ?

Thanks for a reply.

author: Ifmyante
text:
Great '16 to you too!

The ITs, it seems to me, toy around with whatever the hoi polloi are fascinated with at any given time.

If the masses seem to be watching fibs, then the more astute ITs will
spot that, and every once in a while make a fib turn price perfectly.
The retailers jump into the fora and proclaim that fibs are the Holy
Grail, and for a while everybody puts their orders on the fib lines,
only to have their stops taken by the waiting ITs.

If the masses are using median lines, then the big guys may let them hit from time to time too.

We don't need any of that crap though. We can see the manipulation of
the retailers' hopes and fears. When they align with the horizontals we
draw, we strike, and price turns

author: Ifmyante
text:
To take this seriously, we must watch not only our favourite instruments, but also their correlated pairs.

This gives us a better idea of when we should and shouldn't enter.

If say, USD/CAD is at a nice level, but CAD/YEN hasn't yet hit its target, we must wait for both of them to be in position.

I have about ten favourite pairs, but to trade them I'd need to watch perhaps double that amount
